hook-guard.why: Hook commands in a repository's .claude settings run on the machine of anyone who opens an agent session there. A branch can change them; this check holds them to fingerprints kept here, so a changed hook fails CI until the owner adds its fingerprint centrally (Zach, 2026-11-12).

test-tampering.why: Agents that game a task mostly edit its tests (ImpossibleBench; survey issue #1). A PR that deletes or renames away a test file, lowers a test file's assertion count or adds a skip fails unless its body names a decision (DEC-...) or carries a 'Tests-changed-because: <reason>' line (Zach, 2026-11-24: "Make 3, 4, and 5 happen. Approved."; HO-LYD-20261124-SGZN). PRs opened before enforce_from only warn. Dependabot PRs are exempt.

new-dependencies.why: About a fifth of model-suggested packages don't exist (Spracklen et al.; survey issue #5). A PR that adds a package to package.json, pyproject.toml or requirements*.txt must name a decision (DEC-...) in its body, and each new package must exist on PyPI or npm (Zach, 2026-11-24, HO-LYD-20261124-SGZN). Version bumps and lockfile-only changes don't count; Dependabot PRs are exempt. PRs opened before enforce_from only warn, including for a package that doesn't exist.

closing-keywords.why: GitHub closes an issue or PR when a merged PR's description puts a closing keyword (close, fix, resolve and their forms) before a reference to it; Lydian #27 closed itself when #30 merged because #30 said "It closes #27's open security finding". A PR description with such a line fails unless the line carries <!-- intends-close --> (Zach, 2026-11-26 18:02 CT: "1. Yes"; HO-LYD-20261127-HA08). PRs opened before enforce_from only warn. Dependabot PRs are exempt.
